summary: Add audited same-host handoff for idle active task claims
description: The current CLI has no supported way to transfer an active task claim: workspace rebind requires a canonical claim that has already moved, while task review does not transfer an existing owner. Add an explicit same-control-root handoff that verifies exact owner/run/workspace identity and stopped/idle state, preserves dirty work and review metadata, and is resumable across interrupted writes. Do not claim cross-host or independent-clone migration support.
acceptance: A supported `task handoff` CLI transition requires task ID, exact expected old owner, new owner, a non-empty reason, and explicit stopped-owner acknowledgement; registered workspaces also require exact old/new run IDs plus matching stored `control_host` or stopped completion-checkpoint host evidence, while hostless records require `--confirm-same-host` and known mismatches are never overridden.
New workspace records and Git markers persist `control_host`; existing hostless records remain usable only with matching stopped checkpoint evidence or explicit same-host confirmation.

Managed handoff holds the task and workspace-execution locks, preserves workspace path/branch/base/repository identity/generation and dirty file content, and never resets, cleans, or deletes work. Index flags that can hide tracked changes fail closed.

A legacy active task with no registered workspace/run can be handed off only through an explicit `--legacy-unmanaged` path with no run-state conflict; its task status, review status, scope, and content are preserved.
An interrupted handoff is resumable only from exact recorded before/after states; any drift, live/unknown owner, mismatched run, or unregistered foreign workspace fails closed.

Regression tests cover managed and legacy success, live run, wrong owner/run, conflicting state, dirty-work preservation, interrupted recovery, host mismatch, and hostless acknowledgment; registered handoffs require a matching `control_host` or stopped completion checkpoint, hostless records require `--confirm-same-host`, and known mismatches are never waived. Docs exclude cross-host and independent-clone migration.
The public router preserves plan-only authority for Dutch `los … op` intent: `Alleen plan: los het probleem duurzaam op` remains plan-only and non-executing.

review_history.evidence: DEVIL verdict C: prepared-handoff recovery fingerprint omits staged index entry blobs/modes. workspace_content_fingerprint hashes HEAD, porcelain status, changed paths, and working-tree bytes, but a staged index blob can change while worktree bytes/status remain the same; retry may transfer claim despite staged work drift. Fix: deterministically hash staged index entries (avoid raw .git/index stat-cache noise), add regression proving retry fails before task/registry/workspace writes and journal stays prepared; rerun verification and fresh review.

Fresh isolated adversarial probe found C blocker in apply-window race: workspace_content_fingerprint preflight passes, then workspace bytes can change before task/registry writes; the post-write fingerprint rejects but leaves task claim and registry transferred with journal still prepared. Reproduction mutated workspace immediately before task write: error reported, yet task owner=hermes and registry owner=hermes. Must add regression asserting drift during apply rolls ownership metadata back only when exact after-state snapshots match, preserves changed workspace bytes, and otherwise leaves all state untouched/fails closed; verify retry/journal semantics.

Independent Stage 1 spec review PASS and Stage 2 Devil review A on the exact final diff. Stage 2 independently checked transaction recovery and rollback, staged-index fingerprinting, owner/run/liveness gates, dirty-work preservation, tests/docs/scope; no blocking findings. Both reviewers read-only.
